AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Various suboccipital approaches are extensively used in modern neurosurgery for treatment of posterior cranial fossa disease. The main patient's positions on the operating table during surgery are half-sitting and lying ones.

AbstractText.Label: MATERIAL AND METHODS
AbstractText.content: The article provides a detailed description and methodology of retrosigmoid suboccipital and median suboccipital approaches in a lying position.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: The retrosigmoid suboccipital and median suboccipital approaches in a lying position, when used correctly, provide a good view of the operating field with the minimal risk of complications associated with the patient's position on the operating table.
